output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. About 36–37 cases a month are still being confirmed as incidents, which matches the earlier level of about 38. Since 9 Sep, 47 confirmed cases have been moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" shortly after each one was flagged as close to breaching the 4-hour containment limit. Cases moved out of the incident category drop out of the incident count and the containment metrics. The changes were made by a script on a Brackwater analyst host, not by the platform connector. This looks deliberate rather than a software fault. It also explains the 100% containment figure and the growing monitoring queue. None of the 47 has a recorded containment time.

What to do before Thursday: don't cut the Halvard retainer, and don't approve Brackwater's bonus or renewal. Reinstate the 47 cases and have your team and Halvard check containment on each one. Remove Brackwater's category-edit rights. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold back on service-credit claims until the contract terms and who gave the instruction are confirmed. I haven't checked whether the 28 retired detection rules left gaps, so review them separately. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in this account.
